reconcile.connective: Henry keeps the two lines distinct — Libni heading a Gershonite family, Mahli a Merarite one — so the shared name marks two different men in two branches.

discrepancy.connective: Curtis and Madsen, in the standard critical commentary, read these Levitical lists as textually disturbed — treating the Merari-line Libni as scribal duplication, not a second real man.

skeptic.name: Edward L. Curtis and Albert A. Madsen
skeptic.work: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Chronicles (ICC)
skeptic.attribution: Edward L. Curtis (d. 1911) & Albert A. Madsen, A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Books of Chronicles, ICC (Edinburgh: T&T Clark, 1910)

excerpts.excerpt_text: One of the families of Gershom (that of Libni) is here drawn down as far as Samuel, who had the honour of a prophet added to that of a Levite. One of the families of Merari (that of Mahli) is likewise drawn down for several descents …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly handles the two branches in tension: it assigns Libni to the Gershom line and names Mahli (not Libni) as the head of the drawn-out Merari family, supporting the harmonization that the Gershonite Libni and the Merari-line entry are distinct, keeping Libni's father as Gershon.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714), on 1 Chronicles 6
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly, distinguishing the Gershonite family of Libni from the Merarite family of Mahli and so reading the shared name as two different men in two branches.
